correctness.rationale: Read full theorem and proof. Every nonempty dual GP set X must meet each join factor: otherwise a nonedge p,q of an omitted noncomplete factor has a length-two geodesic via any x in X, violating convexity of V\X. Fix an outside-factor x in X: nonadjacent p,q within X in another factor violate general-position, and nonadjacent p,q within V\X violate convexity. Thus both sides induce cliques, and conversely every clique has internal distances one. Equivalent proper complement 2-colorings split independently across connected bipartite components; the product 1+∏(z^a+z^b) is exact, with isolated components z+1. Maximal nonempty solutions include all isolated complement vertices and orient every edge-bearing component; this gives z^u times the reduced product. Verified direct geodesic/2-clique enumeration on several nonuniform joins independently. General proof is not an extrapolation from these examples.
residual_risks: Unproved for joins with complete factors (outside stated theorem); empty set requires separate constant term 1.
Maximal-set formula applies only if complement bipartite and nonempty solutions exist.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge the all-set two-clique equivalence and complete counting polynomial for arbitrary joins of two or more noncomplete factors is distinct from the prior complete-multipartite special case. The directly relevant 2026 journal full text, checked in sections on lexicographic products and final open questions, explicitly lists determining gp_d(K_m o G) as outstanding and gives only conditional/zero cases, not this classification. The new theorem solves it when K_m is complete with m>=2 and H arbitrary noncomplete, and also gives all-set/maximal polynomials.

value.rationale: Determining dual GP sets for complete-first-factor lexicographic products is a directly recorded open natural problem in relevant full-text literature. The theorem resolves it on all finite noncomplete fibers while deriving complete labelled cardinality, maxima and maximal-set generating functions, including examples beyond multipartite graphs. This is a motivated structural classification, not arbitrary numerical slicing.
residual_risks: The simplicity of the final equivalence leaves possible implicit prior cover in general convexity/clique-cover literature; best-of-knowledge priority only.

final_claim: For a join of at least two noncomplete finite graphs, every nonempty dual GP set is exactly one side of a partition into two cliques; such sets exist exactly when the complementary graph is bipartite, with full and inclusion-maximal counting polynomials from its bipartite components.
limitations: All factors noncomplete and at least two; arbitrary first lex product factors excluded.
No claim that finite tests prove the infinite family.
